title: Fats Waller throws her in the air at Connie's Inn
summary: At Connie's Inn a friend bet that she could play everything Fats Waller composed. She did and Waller threw her up in the air; she then talks of the woman pianist Lovey Austin.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yes, he was terrific. Later on in Scranton he
was working in the Cotton Club, Connie's Inn. one Which/was in Harlem?
Connie's Inn. A friend of his took me there and ...He said, "I have a little girl who can play everything you composed." Now this man was a giant. Leonard, the producer, I've forgotten his name -

He said, "All right, Fats, we're ready for the music after you give the girl some routines." I'd say, "O.K." He'd bring out his jug and what-not and he'd say, "What's the title? What you doing?" Leonard would tell him the story. And the man would play it straight off, lyric and everything, a whole 32-bar song... So I was sitting over in the corner. This man had moved there because he was going to put them on, like a bet. He'd say, "This girl can play everything she heard you compose." "She can't!" "I bet you!" So I sat down and played. ( ) and all these other things. Fats took me and threw me up in the air. He grabbed me and threw me up in the air and he bit me and everything. I wished I wasn't even there after all that went on. I thought he was the most amazing woman's pianist, I'm going to do the same thing. What's the/name I told you my brother-in-law used to take me to hear in Pittsburgh? Lovey Austin used to write music and play with her left hand. I used to do that with Andy Kirk.
